before.title: 2.4L Ecotec Excessive Oil Consumption
before.description: Auras with the 2.4L Ecotec four-cylinder (XE) can develop high oil consumption as they age, often attributed to worn piston oil-control rings allowing oil past the rings into the combustion chamber. Owners report burning roughly a quart every 1,000-2,000 miles, which can lead to low-oil conditions and engine wear if not monitored. This is a known weakness across the GM 2.4L Ecotec family.
before.solution: Monitor oil level frequently between changes and top off as needed; severe cases require piston/ring replacement or a short-block. Keeping to high-quality oil and regular change intervals helps. Some owners catch it early via the oil-life monitor and frequent checks.
symptoms: Low oil level between changes
Burning roughly 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles
Low oil pressure / oil light
Blue smoke on startup
Fouled spark plugs

proposal.title: 2.4L Ecotec Excessive Oil Consumption
proposal.description: The 2009 owner manual confirms a 2.4 L engine and tells owners to check oil at each fuel fill. GM diagnostic material defines a controlled threshold for excessive consumption and lists multiple possible causes, including external leaks, incorrect level or viscosity, severe use, crankcase-ventilation faults, valve seals and piston rings. The captured material does not establish a recurring Saturn Aura piston-ring defect, does not prove that all 2007-2009 cars share one non-hybrid 2.4 L configuration and does not support the frozen owner-frequency language. A measured consumption test and leak inspection are required before assigning an internal-engine cause.
proposal.solution: Verify the exact engine and service history, correct any external leak, establish the oil level on level ground using the owner-manual method and document additions over a controlled mileage interval. If consumption exceeds the applicable GM diagnostic guideline, inspect crankcase ventilation and perform leak-down, compression, borescope or other tests as symptoms require before condemning rings, valve seals or the engine. Maintain the specified oil level while testing and stop if oil pressure, overheating or severe running symptoms occur. Do not buy pistons, rings, valve seals, a PCV component or a short block from this page; the engine identity and measured cause must be established first.
symptoms: Oil level repeatedly drops between documented checks
Blue exhaust smoke or oil-fouled spark plugs requiring diagnosis
External oil leakage or crankcase-ventilation fault
Measured consumption exceeding the applicable GM diagnostic threshold
affectedSystems: 2.4 L engine lubrication system
Crankcase ventilation and external seals
Piston rings, cylinders and valve seals, only if testing confirms

before.title: 3.6L Random/Multiple-Cylinder Misfire
before.description: The 3.6L V6 Auras are reported to throw misfire codes, frequently as a downstream symptom of the stretched timing chains but also from worn ignition coils/spark plugs or carbon buildup on the direct-injection intake valves. Owners experience rough idle, hesitation, and a check engine light. P0300 with cylinder-specific misfire codes is common.
before.solution: Diagnose root cause: inspect/measure timing chain deviation first (since chains are a known weak point), then replace spark plugs and any failed ignition coils. Walnut-blast carbon from intake valves if buildup is present. Address timing chains if correlation codes accompany the misfire.
symptoms: Check engine light (often flashing)
Rough idle / shaking
Hesitation or stumble on acceleration
Reduced fuel economy

before.title: 3.6L V6 (LY7) Stretched Timing Chains
before.description: The early GM 3.6L high-feature V6 (used in Aura XR) is prone to premature timing chain stretch, sometimes appearing as early as 50,000-100,000 miles. As the chains wear, camshaft-to-crankshaft timing drifts out of spec, setting correlation codes and eventually causing rough running, reduced power, and potential engine damage if ignored. A cold-start rattle is a common early warning sign.
before.solution: Replace all three timing chains, tensioners, and guides (a major job). GM issued Special Coverage Adjustment #11340 (extending warranty to 10 years/120,000 miles on affected engines and requiring ECM reprogramming in some cases). Use the correct oil and change intervals to slow wear.
symptoms: Check engine light with timing correlation codes
Rattle on cold start
Rough idle / misfire
Reduced power
Engine light flashing under load

before.title: Body Control Module Connection Corrosion (Brake Lights / Cruise)
before.description: Increased resistance can develop in the Body Control Module (BCM) electrical connection on 2008 Auras, causing voltage fluctuations. This can affect exterior lighting (including brake lights), electronic stability control, vehicle speed control (cruise), and related systems, creating intermittent electrical faults. It was significant enough to prompt a safety recall.
before.solution: Covered by NHTSA recall 14V252000 — dealers secured the wiring harness to the BCM with a spacer and applied dielectric lubricant to the connectors. Out of warranty, cleaning/repairing the BCM connector and applying dielectric grease addresses the high-resistance connection.
symptoms: Intermittent or inoperative brake lights
Cruise control cuts out
Stability control / traction control warning lights

proposal.title: Body Control Module Connection Corrosion (Brake Lights / Cruise)

before.title: EVAP Canister Purge Valve Failure (Check Engine Light)
before.description: Auras commonly throw EVAP emissions faults, most often from a stuck-open or failing canister purge solenoid/valve (and sometimes a clogged charcoal canister or faulty fuel-tank pressure sensor). The result is a persistent check engine light and potential emissions-test failure. The gas cap is worth checking first but is usually not the cause of the P0496 flow-during-non-purge code.
before.solution: Confirm the gas cap is tight, inspect EVAP vacuum lines for cracks, then replace the canister purge solenoid/valve if it is stuck open. Replace the charcoal canister or fuel-tank pressure sensor if those are at fault.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Failed emissions/smog test
Occasional rough idle
Fuel odor in some cases

proposal.title: EVAP Canister Purge Valve Failure (Check Engine Light)

Replace only the component that fails its prescribed test and verify the monitor after repair. before.title: Premature Warped Front Brake Rotors
before.description: First-generation Auras (especially 2007) are widely reported to warp their front brake rotors prematurely, producing steering-wheel and front-end shimmy under braking. Owners report rotors warping within a few thousand miles and needing repeated resurfacing or replacement, in some cases every 10,000 miles. The issue was acknowledged by service staff as a design weakness on 2007 and, to a lesser degree, 2008 cars.
before.solution: Replace the rotors and pads; many owners switched to higher-quality aftermarket rotors and pads to reduce recurrence. Proper lug-nut torque (even tightening) and avoiding overheating also helps. The underlying fix is upgraded rotors, as resurfacing alone tends to recur.
symptoms: Steering wheel shakes when braking
Front-end vibration/pulsation under braking
Pedal pulsation
Repeated need to resurface or replace rotors

proposal.title: Premature Warped Front Brake Rotors
proposal.description: GM bulletin 01-05-23-001B provides rotor lateral-runout limits and explicitly says other sources of brake pulsation, including ABS feedback, must be addressed first. The Aura factory manual includes brake-pulsation, rotor/drum balance and vibration diagnostics. Those sources do not establish a recurring 2007-2008 Aura design weakness, do not support replacement every few thousand miles and do not prove that a pulsation is a physically warped front rotor.
proposal.solution: Reproduce the symptom safely and distinguish steering-wheel shake, pedal pulsation, ABS activation and vehicle vibration. Inspect pad and caliper operation, measure rotor thickness variation and lateral runout, and inspect the hub flange, wheel mounting surfaces, bearings and wheel-nut torque before replacing parts. Correct the measured cause and bed new friction components according to their instructions. Do not buy front rotors, pads, calipers or hubs from this page; axle location, dimensions, measured runout and the actual source of pulsation must be established.
symptoms: Brake-pedal pulsation during a repeatable stop
Steering-wheel shake requiring axle-source isolation
Measured rotor thickness variation or lateral runout
ABS feedback or wheel/tire vibration mistaken for rotor distortion

before.title: Transmission Shift Cable Fracture (Rollaway Risk)
before.description: The plastic shift cable end fitting or its retaining tabs can wear out and fracture on automatic-transmission Auras. When this happens, the gear indicator may show 'Park' (or the wrong gear) while the transmission is actually still in Drive, Reverse, or Neutral, and the driver may be unable to shift to Park or remove the key. This created a serious vehicle rollaway hazard and was linked to multiple crashes and injuries. It is the single most-documented and safety-critical defect on the Aura, addressed by two NHTSA recalls.
before.solution: Covered by recall (NHTSA 12V460000 installed a retainer over the cable end; 14V224000 replaced the shift cable assembly and mounting bracket at no charge). Out of warranty, the fix is to replace the shift cable/shifter cable bushing or full cable assembly; some cases are resolved by replacing the small worn plastic bushing where the cable connects to the transmission lever.
symptoms: Shifter shows Park but car can still roll
Cannot shift lever into Park

proposal.title: Transmission Shift Cable Fracture (Rollaway Risk)
proposal.description: GM recall 12V460/12106 covers VIN-selected 2007-2010 Saturn Aura vehicles equipped with a four-speed automatic transmission whose shift-cable end-fitting tabs may fracture and separate, allowing the indicated shifter position to differ from the transmission gear and creating rollaway risk. Recall 14V224/14152 addressed an additional cable failure population with cable-and-bracket replacement. Campaign materials do not authorize substituting a retail bushing for the VIN-specific remedy.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for open campaigns 12V460 and 14V224 before repair. If the shifter position does not match actual gear, the vehicle cannot be secured in Park or the key/indicator behaves abnormally, set the parking brake, keep people clear of the vehicle path and arrange safe towing or dealer instructions. An authorized dealer should perform the current campaign remedy for an involved VIN. Do not buy a shift-cable bushing, cable, bracket or retainer from this page; VIN campaign, transmission RPO, cable design and inspection determine the remedy.
